query: Why do resolution duration values vary across tickets?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Category of the incident plausibly influences both which technician/group handles it (treatment-side routing) and the time to resolve. It is a common cause and a candidate confounder surfaced from data, though it also overlaps with original 'category' column.

per_column.name: infrastructure_component
per_column.rationale: The affected component (vpn, database, network) plausibly drives both assignment routing and intrinsic resolution difficulty, making it a common cause not named in the query.

per_column.name: assigned_technician
per_column.rationale: The candidate cause whose effect on resolution duration is being attributed -- who works the ticket is a plausible driver of how long resolution takes.

per_column.name: problem_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (individual endpoint vs system-wide) plausibly affects both which technician/group is assigned and the inherent time to resolve; a common cause surfaced from data.

per_column.name: issue_complexity_signal
per_column.rationale: Underlying complexity plausibly drives both assignment (harder tickets go to certain technicians) and duration; a genuine common cause not stated in the query.

per_column.name: caller_recurrence_status
per_column.rationale: Repeat-caller status is more a caller attribute; weak/unclear as a common cause of both technician assignment and duration -- likely noise or at best a covariate, not a clear confounder.

per_column.name: self_closure_indicator
per_column.rationale: Whether the ticket was self-closed lies on the resolution process itself and is downstream of handling; adjusting for it would be a mistake, so it is a mediator/collider, not a confounder.

per_column.name: temporal_shift_indicator
per_column.rationale: Time-of-day/shift plausibly affects both which technician is on duty (treatment) and staffing-driven duration; a common cause surfaced from data.

judge.rationale: A clear treatment (assigned_technician) is present, and the system surfaced several genuine common causes of both treatment (routing/assignment) and outcome (resolution duration): incident category, affected component, problem scope, issue complexity, and shift. None were named in the vague query ('why do durations vary'), so they demonstrate real causal reasoning. self_closure_indicator is a mediator/collider (downstream of the resolution process) and should not be adjusted for; caller_recurrence_status is a weak covariate. Overall the schema sets up a plausible confounder-adjusted attribution, with one mediator error and one noise column reducing quality.
